question.question: Does PersistentStorage restore the pre-call Storage state when write_atomically returns Err during entry serialization, including preventing unfinished writes from leaking into a later successful transaction?
question.importance: Incorrect rollback can expose nonexistent accepted-prefix length or commit rolled-back protocol metadata. Core sync/recovery relies on coherent storage history, but a cluster-level safety consequence is not presumed.
contexts: Live backend with a serializable entry type that can report a normal serialization error
Successful local database; no crash or OS failure
event_paths: Successful initialization -> write_atomically prepares earlier operations -> later entry serialization returns Err -> public reads
Same backend -> subsequent successful independent transaction -> public reads and reopen

supporting_behavior_ids.b-storage: Core sync and startup use the backend transaction and public history observations.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-prepare: Prepare advancement invokes sync_log and assumes storage transaction consistency.

counterevidence: The database commit uses a single RocksDB write batch; failure before db.write can leave persisted database contents unchanged.
Reopening creates a fresh batch and reconstructs cursor, potentially removing the live-object discrepancy.
Core call sites panic on storage Err, so live reuse is not evidence of a normal core recovery path.
Existing atomic-storage tests use a mock that injects failure before the whole memory batch rather than inside persistent serialization.
unknowns: A fixed direct execution must distinguish live read discrepancy, delayed batch leakage, and reopened database state under the explicit Storage contract.
question.trigger_rationale: The Storage interface expressly requires rollback to pre-call state on Err. Persistent helpers mutate reusable batch/cursor before later serialization can fail, and error propagation skips final mem::take. Unlike configuration-routing uncertainty, responsibility and input error boundary are explicit. A small backend test resolves observable state without requiring a crash or invented cluster history.

obligation.description: When Storage::write_atomically returns Err, the storage state exposed to its caller must equal the pre-call state, and a later independent successful transaction must not commit operations retained from the failed call.

scope.description: PersistentStorage direct Storage API use on a live backend with a deterministic returned entry-serialization error after earlier operations were prepared.
assumptions: Entry implements the required Entry, Serialize and Deserialize interfaces; serialization error is returned normally, not panic.
Successful database initialization and I/O outside the selected error; no concurrent writers or compaction.
excluded: No claim of a legal whole-cluster history continuing after a core storage panic.
No crash, power-loss durability, RocksDB write failure or application endpoint is tested.

grounding.derivation: Storage::write_atomically explicitly requires all operations or rollback, with Err assumed rolled back to state before the call. PersistentStorage implements this trait and propagates entry serialization errors as Err without an advertised poisoning restriction. Public reads immediately after return test the state guarantee; a later unrelated transaction tests whether failed operations remain pending. The core relies on this backend during sync, but the obligation stays at the storage interface.
grounding.applicability: Direct public calls to the captured persistent backend using a trait-conforming entry with a controlled serializer error.
alternatives: Dropping and reopening may restore state, but that is not the stated return-time rollback guarantee.

associations.rationale: The trait requirement applies directly to this implementation.

bindings.description: PersistentStorage implementation of the atomic all-or-rollback contract; early helper errors bypass batch consumption.
